October 23, 2026

To
The Director General
Department of Immigration and Passports
Agargaon, Dhaka-1207.

**Subject: Application for administrative and financial sanction to procure 10 units of Online UPS and precision air conditioning units for regional server rooms.**

Sir,

During recent technical performance audits, it was observed that frequent commercial power grid fluctuations and extreme summer ambient temperatures have caused repeated server thermal throttling and damaged several SMPS units. 1. 10 units of 6 KVA True Online Double-Conversion UPS (with 2-hour battery backup).

A detailed technical specification sheet and an estimated budget of BDT 35,00,000 (Thirty-Five Lakh Taka only) have been prepared in compliance with the Public Procurement Rules (PPR-2008) and are attached herewith for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently,

*(Signature)*

answer:

DEPARTMENT OF IMMIGRATION AND PASSPORTS
ICT & INFORMATION SECURITY CELL
Headquarters, E-7 Agargaon, Dhaka-1207

MEMORANDUM

Ref No: 44.01.0000.701.12.008.26-112
Date: 23 October 2026

TO: All Assistant Directors, Maintenance Engineers & Data Entry Supervisors
    Regional Passport Offices (All)

SUBJECT: MANDATORY ENFORCEMENT OF TWO-FACTOR AUTHENTICATION (2FA) AND STRICT CLEAN DESK POLICY FOR ALL BIOMETRIC ENROLLMENT TERMINALS

1. Recent national vulnerability assessments indicate that credential theft and unauthorized terminal access represent the highest threat vectors targeting citizen identity databases. To fortify our Critical Information Infrastructure against illicit intrusion, the following security directives are hereby promulgated for immediate and strict compliance:

   (a) **Mandatory 2FA Enforcement:** Effective from 01 November 2026, no operator shall access the e-Passport Central Portal using single-factor static passwords. Access will strictly require user credentials paired with a hardware FIDO2 Security Token or mobile-based authenticator OTP.
   (b) **Clean Desk and Clear Screen Policy:** All enrollment desks must remain clear of physical applicant files, handwritten passport numbers, or removable media (USB drives) when unattended. Workstations must be configured to lock automatically after two (02) minutes of inactivity.
   (c) **Prohibition of Unauthorized Hardware:** Under no circumstances shall personal smartphones, external webcams, or unauthorized Wi-Fi dongles be connected to the government network switch or PC USB ports.

2. Regional Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineers are instructed to conduct bi-weekly audit sweeps and log terminal compliance. Any breach of this directive will trigger disciplinary action under the Government Servants (Conduct) Rules.

By Order of the Director General,

(Signature)
(Engr. Tanvir Ahmed)
Director (Systems & ICT)
Department of Immigration and Passports, Dhaka.

**1. INCIDENT OVERVIEW:**  
On the night of 22 October 2026 at 21:42 hours, an unauthorized entry attempt was recorded at the biometric magnetic access door of Central Server Room (Zone-A). The automated security controller triggered a silent alarm to the Security Operations Center (SOC). question: As a Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer, write a formal 'Technical Incident & Downtime Report' addressed to the System Analyst regarding a major network outage at the Regional Passport Office caused by a broadcast storm/switching loop. Outline root cause, immediate recovery actions, and long-term preventive measures.
answer:
Model Technical Incident Report:

TECHNICAL INCIDENT REPORT

Reference: DIP/RPO-DHK/INC-2026/089
Date: 23 October 2026
To: System Analyst, ICT Division, Department of Immigration & Passports
From: Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer, Regional Passport Office
Subject: Incident Post-Mortem Report: 90-Minute Network Downtime at Enrollment LAN

1. Executive Summary:
On 23 October 2026 at 10:15 AM, the local area network (LAN) serving all 14 biometric enrollment counters and the citizen queue display system experienced a total outage. Normal operations were fully restored by 11:45 AM (total downtime: 90 minutes).

2. Incident Timeline & Symptoms:
• 10:15 AM: Enrollment workstations reported disconnection from the local verification server; network latency spiked above 4,000 ms with 95% packet drop.
• 10:30 AM: Physical inspection of the core distribution switch (Cisco Catalyst 2960X) revealed 100% CPU utilization and simultaneous flashing of all port activity LEDs (classic broadcast storm indicator).

3. Root Cause Analysis:
An unauthorized patch cord was accidentally cross-connected between two access ports on Switch Rack-02 during routine desk rearrangement by floor support staff. Because Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) BPDU Guard was globally disabled on access-layer edge ports, an active Layer-2 loop formed instantly, generating overwhelming broadcast traffic.

4. Immediate Remediation:
• The redundant looping patch cable was identified and physically disconnected at 10:50 AM.
• Switch CPU loads normalized within 3 minutes; all core IP services and DHCP leases were validated.
• All 14 client workstations successfully resumed biometric enrollment and MRZ submissions by 11:45 AM.

5. Corrective & Preventive Measures:
• Globally enabled Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP) with PortFast and BPDU Guard on all client-facing switch ports.
• Physically locked unused RJ-45 wall ports using port blockers to prevent unauthorized interconnects.
• Scheduled a technical refresher session on rack cabling protocols for support personnel.

Submitted by:
(Signature)
Md. Rafiqul Islam
Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer

question: Draft a comprehensive 'Network Incident & Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Report' addressed to the Director (ICT) concerning an unexpected core distribution switch failure that caused a 45-minute outage at the central passport issuance division.
answer:
Network Incident Report:

**DEPARTMENT OF IMMIGRATION & PASSPORTS**
**ICT & INFRASTRUCTURE WING, HEADQUARTERS, DHAKA**

**INCIDENT REPORT & ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS (RCA)**

**Incident Reference:** INC-2026-1023-NET-01
**Date of Report:** October 23, 2026
**To:** Director (ICT), Department of Immigration and Passports
**From:** Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer, Network & Data Center Operations
**Classification:** Severity-1 (High Impact)

**1. Executive Summary:**
On October 23, 2026, at 10:15 AM, the Central Passport Personalization Division experienced an unexpected network outage lasting 45 minutes (10:15 AM to 11:00 AM). The outage temporarily halted passport printing and personalization queuing. Service was fully restored at 11:00 AM following emergency hardware bypass.

**2. Incident Timeline:**
• **10:15 AM:** Core Distribution Switch (Cisco Catalyst 9500) abruptly rebooted and entered a boot-loop.
• **10:18 AM:** Monitoring system (Zabbix) raised high-priority alerts regarding unreachable subnets (VLAN 30 & VLAN 40).
• **10:25 AM:** Maintenance engineers inspected the rack and observed redundant power supply failure (PSU-2 dead, PSU-1 overheating trip).
• **10:35 AM:** Hot-standby switch was configured, and primary fiber uplinks were patched to the redundant switch.
• **10:50 AM:** Spanning-tree protocol (RSTP) converged; database connectivity re-established.
• **11:00 AM:** Full verification completed; all personalization lines resumed normal operation.

**3. Root Cause Analysis (RCA):**
The primary root cause was an internal capacitor breakdown within Power Supply Unit 2 (PSU-2), which produced a power surge that tripped the thermal protection sensor of PSU-1. The automatic hardware failover failed because PSU-1 drew excessive thermal load due to dust accumulation in the secondary fan chassis.

**4. Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA):**
1. Replaced both faulty power supply modules with genuine OEM redundant units.
2. Implemented active dual-bus UPS power feeds (Feed A from Online UPS-1, Feed B from Online UPS-2).
3. Scheduled bi-weekly physical air-flow and temperature inspections across all core distribution racks.
4. Configured SNMP trap alerting for switch fan RPM and PSU thermal fluctuations.

**Submitted by:**
*(Signature)*
Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer
Department of Immigration and Passports

question: Draft an executive Technical Incident & Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Report concerning a 45-minute total network outage at a Regional Passport Office caused by a physical switching loop and Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) misconfiguration.
answer:
Executive Technical Incident & Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Report:

**DOCUMENT CLASSIFICATION:** INTERNAL RESTRICTED  
**INCIDENT TRACKING ID:** INC-2026-1023-NET  
**AFFECTED FACILITY:** Regional Passport Office, Sylhet  
**DATE OF INCIDENT:** 23 October 2026 | **DURATION:** 45 Minutes (10:15 AM – 11:00 AM)  

**1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:**  
At 10:15 AM, the local area network serving twenty-two (22) biometric enrollment counters and eight (8) delivery stations experienced a total connectivity failure. Applicants could not be enrolled, and e-Gate verification timed out. Full service was restored at 11:00 AM following the isolation of a loop and configuration of Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP).

**2. TIMELINE OF EVENTS:**  
• **10:15 AM:** Core Switch CPU utilization surged to 100%; inter-VLAN ping latency spiked from 1ms to over 3500ms, followed by 98% packet loss.  
• **10:25 AM:** Maintenance Engineer diagnosed a broadcast radiation storm (over 120,000 broadcast packets/sec) saturating all trunk ports.  
• **10:40 AM:** Physical inspection identified that an unmanaged 8-port desktop switch in the training room had both ends of a patch cable inadvertently plugged into two adjacent wall ports connected to Access Switch-02.  
• **10:45 AM:** Loop cable physically disconnected; broadcast storm ceased immediately.  
• **10:55 AM:** Spanning Tree BPDU Guard and Loop Guard enabled globally across all access ports.  
• **11:00 AM:** Full system operational verification confirmed; incident resolved.

**3. ROOT CAUSE:**  
1. **Human Error:** An operator mistakenly connected both ends of an Ethernet patch cable into two live data jacks, forming a physical bridging loop.  
2. **Configuration Gap:** Access Switch-02 had 'BPDU Guard' disabled on edge ports. Consequently, when loop frames circulated, the switch failed to automatically err-disable the rogue port, precipitating an uncontained Layer-2 broadcast storm.

**4. PREVENTIVE ACTIONS & RECOMMENDATIONS:**  
• Enable `spanning-tree portfast bpduguard default` on all edge ports across all switches nationwide.  
• Enforce strict physical port locking on unallocated wall sockets.  
• Deploy automated SNMP trap alerts to notify the NOC when switch CPU exceeds 80%.

**SUBMITTED BY:**  
(Md. Shakil Hossain)  
Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer  
Regional Passport Office, Sylhet.
